name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q01 - Sequence of water flow in sponge canal system

questiontext.text:
Given below are the events and pathways associated with water transport through the canal system of a sponge (Phylum Porifera):

(I) Water exits the body through a large terminal opening called the osculum.
(II) Ambient water containing food and dissolved oxygen enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall.
(III) Choanocytes (collar cells) lining the cavity trap food particles and facilitate respiratory exchange.
(IV) Water enters the central spacious cavity called the spongocoel.

Which of the following represents the correct logical sequence of water flow through the sponge body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Sponges possess a characteristic water canal (water transport) system that functions in nutrition (food gathering), gas exchange (respiratory exchange), and excretion (removal of metabolic wastes).

Step 2: Pathway Evaluation:
Water transport begins when external surrounding water is drawn through numerous microscopic perforations in the body wall, designated as ostia. Therefore, event (II) is the initial step.

Step 3: Internal Circulation:
From the ostia, the water currents pass directly through the body wall into the extensive central internal chamber known as the spongocoel. Thus, event (IV) directly follows event (II).

Step 4: Cellular Filtration:
The spongocoel and internal canals are lined with specialized flagellated cells termed choanocytes (collar cells). As water circulates across the spongocoel, the beating flagella of choanocytes create currents, entrap microscopic food particles for intracellular digestion, and mediate dissolved gas exchange. Hence, event (III) occurs while water traverses the spongocoel.

Step 5: Discharge and Final Answer:
After nutrient absorption and metabolic waste collection, the filtered water stream flows toward the osculum, a large excurrent pore through which water is expelled to the outside. Thus, event (I) represents the terminal step. The complete chronological sequence of flow is (II) → (IV) → (III) → (I).

Final Answer:
(II) → (IV) → (III) → (I)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_MCQ_Q02 - Chronological sequence of cyclostome life cycle

questiontext.text:
Consider the following biological events in the life cycle of living jawless vertebrates belonging to Class Cyclostomata (e.g., Petromyzon):

(I) Death of the spent adult within a few days.
(II) Migration of mature marine adults into freshwater rivers for spawning.
(III) Metamorphosis of the ammocoete larva in freshwater.
(IV) Spawning of gametes in the river bed.
(V) Return of the metamorphosed juvenile to the marine habitat.

Which of the following displays the correct chronological sequence of these events?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
All living members of Class Cyclostomata are marine ectoparasites on fishes that exhibit anadromous migratory behavior for the purpose of sexual reproduction and spawning.

Step 2: Spawning Migration:
Sexually mature adult cyclostomes leave their marine feeding grounds and migrate upstream into freshwater river systems to locate suitable spawning grounds. Thus, event (II) is the initial reproductive event.

Step 3: Gamete Deposition and Adult Mortality:
In freshwater, the adults release their gametes during spawning (event IV). Following this intense reproductive expenditure, the physiological deterioration is severe, and the parent adults die within a few days (event I). Hence, event (IV) is immediately succeeded by event (I).

Step 4: Larval Metamorphosis:
The fertilized eggs develop through indirect development into morphologically distinct larvae (ammocoetes) that inhabit freshwater sediments. After a prolonged filter-feeding period, the larva undergoes metamorphosis into a juvenile form with adult characteristics (event III).

Step 5: Oceanic Return and Final Answer:
Following the completion of metamorphosis, the young juveniles swim downstream and return to the ocean to resume ectoparasitic feeding on marine fishes (event V). Arranging the stages in chronological sequence yields: (II) → (IV) → (I) → (III) → (V).

Final Answer:
(II) → (IV) → (I) → (III) → (V)
